l-selenomethodionine and Se- methylseleno-l- cysteine can be determined using a thiol-modified gold electrode in a flow-through voltammeter.
l-selenomethylselenocysteine and selenomethionin can be determined by a voltammetric method using a flow-through cell.

the electrochemical oxidation of l-selenoamino acids at thiol-compound modified gold electrodes can be used in a flow-through voltammetric detector for the determination of l-seleniumamino acids in commercial selenium-containing supplements.

the application of thiol/gold electrodes as electrochemical detectors in flow-through voltammetry.
a new method for the determination of l-selenium-containing amino acids using high-performance liquid chromotography and a flow-through voltammeter.
the application of a voltammetric sensor for the determination of l-selenium amino acids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electrochemical detection is more sensitive and selective for l-seleno-methionine and for Se-methylselenium-cysteine than the UV detection.
the flow-through voltammetry is a suitable method for the determination of l-selenium-containing amino acids in commercial products.
a flow-through voltammeter is suitable for the detection of l-selenoamino acids, but the detection of Se-methylselenium compounds is not possible.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thiol/gold electrode has the advantage of a high sensitivity for the determination of l-selnomethionine, Se-methylselenium-l-cysteinate, and other selenium compounds in a complex matrix.
the flow-through voltammetry is a suitable method for determining selenium in selenium-containing products.
the thiol-modified gold electrodes have a higher efficiency in the oxidation of l-selenometionine and Se-ethylseleno- l-cysteines compared to a bare gold electrode.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thiol-compound/gold electrodes can be used in voltammetric detectors for the detection and determination of l-selenium-containing amino acids.
thiol compounds can be used as a new class of electrochemical modifiers to increase the sensitivity of the voltammetric detection of l-selenoamino acids.
a flow-through voltammeter can be used to identify l-selenium-containing amino acids and to quantify them.
